messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a complete, playable otome game with customizable protagonist, multiple romance routes, meaningful choices, and an interesting world.
- Make the illustrated characters feel alive with subtle movement, blinking, and facial expressions that respond to emotion.

## Requirements
- Let players choose whether their character is isekai’d or native to the world.
- Support diverse skin tones, eye colors and shapes, hair colors and styles, and pronouns.
- Include attractive male leads, multiple visuals, and choices throughout scenes.
- Character expressions should change with emotion; characters should blink and move subtly.

## Decisions
- The game is titled **Ever After, Elsewhere**, set in the city of Vesper, with three romance leads: Aster Vale, Ren Amari, and Soren Lune.
- Implemented portraits and scene art as inline SVG/CSS rather than relying on external image assets.

## Work State
### Completed
- Created the game shell, responsive styling, character creator, world-origin choice, story scenes, three romance routes, choices, affinity values, and endings.
- Added initial SVG character illustrations and scenic backgrounds.

### Active
- Implement emotional expressions and animation: the latest edit adds mood-dependent `brows` and `mouth` variables in `personSvg()` but does not yet render them or connect moods to story choices.
- Verify and fix the game in a browser; no screenshot or gameplay testing has been done.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Finish `personSvg()` to use mood-dependent brows and mouth, and add animated blinking and subtle idle movement through CSS.
2. Set expressions for the player and route characters as story choices/dialogue change; ensure the face and body animations are visible in the scene.
3. Run the game and test the creator, route choices, expressions, and ending; fix any issues discovered.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game page structure and script/style references.
- `style.css`: Layout, responsive styling, scene visuals, and character presentation.
- `game.js`: Game logic, SVG character drawing, story content, route choices, and current incomplete expression work.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- In `game.js`, the latest `personSvg()` edit defines `brows` and `mouth` based on `opts.mood`, but the SVG still uses hard-coded brow and mouth paths; no blinking or facial/body animation has been implemented yet.

## Objective
- Complete **Ever After, Elsewhere**, a playable otome game with customizable protagonist, romance routes, meaningful choices, and an engaging world.
- Make characters feel alive through subtle movement, blinking, and emotion-responsive expressions.

## Requirements
- Let players choose whether they are isekai’d or native to the world.
- Support diverse skin tones, eye colors and shapes, hair colors and styles, and pronouns.
- Include attractive male leads, multiple visuals, and choices throughout scenes.
- Character expressions should change with emotion; characters should blink and move subtly.

## Decisions
- Title: **Ever After, Elsewhere**; setting: Vesper; romance leads: Aster Vale, Ren Amari, and Soren Lune.
- Character portraits and scene art use inline SVG/CSS rather than external image assets.

### Completed
- Built the responsive game shell, character creator, origin choice, story scenes, three romance routes, choices, affinity values, and endings.
- Added SVG character illustrations and scenic backgrounds.
- Connected mood-dependent brows and mouths to portraits; story choices update player and route-character expressions.
- Added idle breathing, hair sway, blinking, and reduced-motion support.
- `node --check game.js` and `git diff --check` pass; Chromium headless loaded the page and rendered the creator screen.

2. Fix any issues discovered during gameplay testing.

- `game.js`: Game logic, portraits, expressions, animations’ mood inputs, story choices, and endings.
- `style.css`: Layout, scene visuals, character animations, and reduced-motion rules.
- `index.html`: Game page structure and script/style references.

- Changes are uncommitted; the game files are currently untracked.
- Browser verification so far only confirmed the initial creator screen renders; interactive gameplay has not been tested.

- Complete **Ever After, Elsewhere**, a playable otome game with customizable protagonist, meaningful choices, multiple romance routes, and lively characters.
- Expand the game to five male romance leads and add relationship progression with other characters, including friendship and best-friend levels.

- Let players choose whether they are isekai’d or native to Vesper.
- Support diverse skin tones, eye colors and shapes, hair colors and styles, and pronouns.
- Provide at least five male romance leads, each with a dateable route.
- Include other characters whose relationships can grow through friendship to best friends.
- Make expressions respond to emotion and add subtle blinking and movement.

## Decisions
- Title: **Ever After, Elsewhere**; setting: Vesper.
- Existing romance leads: Aster Vale, Ren Amari, and Soren Lune.
- Character portraits and scene art use inline SVG/CSS.

### Completed
- Built the responsive game shell, creator, origin choice, story choices, affinity values, and endings.
- Added SVG character illustrations, scenic backgrounds, mood-responsive expressions, idle animation, and reduced-motion support.
- Fixed and browser-tested prologue → route menu → route introduction → story → ending navigation, plus route switching and restart.

### Active
- Expand the romance roster from three to five male leads and implement their complete dateable routes.
- Implement non-romance character relationships with friendship and best-friend progression.
- Re-test the game after the latest relationship-state changes.

- (none)

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Game content, character data, creator, relationship state, scenes, navigation, and endings.
- `style.css`: Layout, scene visuals, responsive styling, and character animations.
- `index.html`: Game page structure and script/style references.

## Important Context
- Current romance leads are `aster`, `ren`, and `soren`; the latest edit added `luca` and `idris` affinity/expression keys but not their lead definitions or routes.
- Latest edit also added initial `friendship` state for `tavi` and `nessa`, plus `activeFriend`; no friendship gameplay is implemented yet.
- Game files are uncommitted and untracked.

## Objective
- Complete **Ever After, Elsewhere** as a playable otome game with customizable protagonist, five romance routes, and friendships that can grow into best-friend relationships.
- Add a homepage where players choose which male lead appears in the interface, an in-world phone with apps and character messaging, and a customizable photo-shoot mode.

## Requirements
- Let players choose whether they are isekai’d or native to Vesper.
- Support diverse skin tones, eye colors and shapes, hair colors and styles, and pronouns.
- Include at least five dateable male leads and selectable route options.
- Include non-romance friendships that progress through Friends, Close Friends, and Best Friends.
- Make expressions respond to emotion and add subtle blinking and movement.
- Add a homepage with a selectable male lead for the interface.
- Add a phone with multiple apps, including messaging that lets the player contact characters from Vesper.
- Add photo shoots with one, two, or all characters, configurable poses, clothes, accessories, backgrounds, effects, and camera view.

## Decisions
- Title: **Ever After, Elsewhere**; setting: Vesper.
- Romance leads: Aster Vale, Ren Amari, Soren Lune, Luca Bellamy, and Idris Thorne.
- Friendship characters: Tavi Rowan and Nessa Quill.
- Character portraits and scene art use inline SVG/CSS.

## Work State
### Completed
- Built the responsive game shell, protagonist creator, origin choice, story choices, affinity values, romance endings, illustrated scenes, mood-responsive expressions, idle animation, and reduced-motion support.
- Added Luca and Idris romance data and endings.
- Added Tavi and Nessa friendship data, route-menu cards, choice progression, and relationship tiers.
- Added friend-scene rendering and menu-to-friend navigation code.

### Active
- Build the requested homepage/interface-lead selection, in-world phone and messaging apps, and customizable photo-shoot mode.
- Test five romance and friendship flows end-to-end, including verifying relationship state and scene presentation.
- Check responsive presentation of expanded route/friend cards and new interface features.

- (none)

1. Inspect current `game.js`, `index.html`, and `style.css` structure, then implement the homepage, selectable interface lead, phone/apps and messaging, and photo-shoot customization.
2. Test all five romance routes through endings and Tavi/Nessa progression through Best Friends; verify the new features and responsive layouts in a browser.
3. Re-run `node --check game.js` and `git diff --check`.

- `style.css`: Layout, scene visuals, responsive styling, and character animations.

- Let players choose whether they are isekai’d or native to Vesper.

## Objective
- Complete **Ever After, Elsewhere** as a playable otome game with customizable protagonist, five romance routes, and friendships that can grow into best-friend relationships.
- Validate the homepage, phone, photo studio, story flows, built-in character voices, and responsive layouts.

## Requirements
- Let players choose whether they are isekai’d or native to Vesper.
- Support diverse appearances and pronouns, five dateable male leads, and selectable routes.
- Support friendships progressing through Friends, Close Friends, and Best Friends.
- Include expressive characters with subtle blinking and movement.
- Provide homepage interface-lead selection, in-world phone apps and messaging, customizable photo studio, built-in character speech and emotional reactions, and many clothing options.

## Decisions
- Title: **Ever After, Elsewhere**; setting: Vesper.
- Romance leads: Aster Vale, Ren Amari, Soren Lune, Luca Bellamy, Idris Thorne; friends: Tavi Rowan and Nessa Quill.
- Character portraits and scene art use inline SVG/CSS; dialogue playback uses browser speech synthesis.

## Work State
### Completed
- Built the responsive game shell, protagonist creator, origin choice, story choices, affinity values, romance endings, illustrated scenes, expressions, idle animation, and reduced-motion support.
- Added five romance routes, two friendship progressions, and Home, Phone, Photo Studio, and Story navigation.
- Added phone apps, local character message threads, interface-lead selection, and photo-shoot customization with 12 outfits.
- Added speech controls and mood-dependent delivery, including `hurt` and `excited`.
- Verified homepage, creator with native origin/customization, all five romance routes through endings, and friendship progress: Tavi reached Best Friends; Nessa reached Close Friends.
- Verified messaging and reply, journal, bonds display, and photo customization controls.
- Fixed the journal’s unnamed-player heading and cleared previous photo-studio classes on entry.
- `node --check game.js` and `git diff --check` passed before the subsequent browser test command encountered a Playwright-script syntax error.

### Active
- Validate voice playback and emotional expression visuals; finish responsive desktop/mobile checks.
- Recheck photo studio after its class-reset fix and finish final validation.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Verify voice toggle and playback, plus character expressions for hurt/excited moments.
2. Check desktop and mobile layouts and retest photo studio class reset.
3. Rerun syntax and diff checks; investigate the existing `/favicon.ico` 404 if appropriate.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Game state, routes, phone, photo studio, expressions, and speech synthesis.
- `index.html`: Game structure, navigation, and voice toggle.
- `features.css`: Homepage, phone, and photo-studio styling.
- `style.css`: Layout, scenes, responsive styling, and animations.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files are untracked in git.
- Friendship thresholds are score 1 = Friends, 3 = Close Friends, and 6 = Best Friends.
- Playwright is open at `http://localhost:3002`; the known console error is a missing `/favicon.ico` (404), with no other errors or warnings reported.

## Objective
- Complete **Ever After, Elsewhere** as a playable otome game with customizable protagonist, five romance routes, and friendships that can grow into best-friend relationships.
- Validate the homepage, phone, photo studio, story flows, built-in character voices, expressions, and responsive layouts.

## Requirements
- Let players choose whether they are isekai’d or native to Vesper.
- Support diverse appearances and pronouns, five dateable male leads, and selectable routes.
- Support friendships progressing through Friends, Close Friends, and Best Friends.
- Include expressive characters with subtle blinking and movement.
- Provide homepage interface-lead selection, in-world phone apps and messaging, customizable photo studio, character speech and emotional reactions, and many clothing options.

## Decisions
- Title: **Ever After, Elsewhere**; setting: Vesper.
- Romance leads: Aster Vale, Ren Amari, Soren Lune, Luca Bellamy, Idris Thorne; friends: Tavi Rowan and Nessa Quill.
- Character portraits and scene art use inline SVG/CSS; dialogue playback uses browser speech synthesis.

## Work State
### Completed
- Built the responsive game shell, protagonist creator, origin choice, story choices, affinity values, romance endings, illustrated scenes, expressions, idle animation, and reduced-motion support.
- Added five romance routes, two friendship progressions, and Home, Phone, Photo Studio, and Story navigation.
- Added phone apps, local character message threads, interface-lead selection, and photo-shoot customization with 12 outfits.
- Added speech controls and mood-dependent delivery, including `hurt` and `excited`.
- Verified homepage, creator with native origin/customization, all five romance routes through endings, and friendship progress: Tavi reached Best Friends; Nessa reached Close Friends.
- Verified messaging/replies, journal, bonds, and photo controls; fixed the unnamed journal heading and photo-studio class reset on entry.
- Verified voice toggle and playback, distinct excited/hurt expressions, photo studio class reset, and desktop/mobile layouts with no horizontal overflow.
- Added SVG favicon reference and updated sound-toggle accessibility label/state to describe character voices.
- `node --check game.js` and `git diff --check` passed before the latest HTML-only edits.

### Active
- Final validation of the favicon and recent voice-toggle markup changes; rerun syntax and diff checks.

1. Confirm `favicon.svg` exists and loads; inspect browser console for any remaining errors.
2. Rerun `node --check game.js` and `git diff --check`, then verify the voice-toggle label and behavior.
3. Review final `git status`; all project files are untracked and changes are uncommitted.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Game state, routes, phone, photo studio, expressions, and speech synthesis.
- `index.html`: Game structure, navigation, voice toggle, and favicon link.
- `features.css`: Homepage, phone, and photo-studio styling.
- `style.css`: Layout, scenes, responsive styling, and animations.

- Playwright is open at `http://localhost:3002`; earlier the only reported console issue was a missing `/favicon.ico` (404), and a `favicon.svg` link was just added but not yet checked.
- The speech-synthesis test intercepted `speak` and observed playback; the toggle click also automatically spoke the current dialogue, so the recorded line appeared twice after clicking the line button.
- Friendship thresholds are score 1 = Friends, 3 = Close Friends, and 6 = Best Friends.
